title: Focus sprint lens — weekly heuristics & measurement
content:
Purpose: quick, low-friction weekly lens to keep the sprint of habits and outcome-focused work on track. Not an OKR doc, not a polished plan — think of this as the living scratchpad and signal filter for the week.

Structure (start here each Monday, 10–15m):
1) Northline — single sentence outcome this week (what I will judge at the end).
   - Example: Increase insight-generating prompts in my notes by 30% so I have 6 better rewrite candidates for the monthly write-up.

2) Three heuristics to prioritize (fast checks to gate work):
   - Heuristic A: Does this directly increase signal (more examples, fewer vague bullets)? If no, deprioritize.
   - Heuristic B: Is it small enough to finish in a single focused slot (30–90m)? If not, break it.
   - Heuristic C: Does this reduce friction later (templates, tiny automations)? If yes, bump up.

3) Weekly commitments (3 items max):
   - Commitment 1: Run one micro-audit of notes from last month (identify 3 candidate prompts).
   - Commitment 2: Ship a one-pager template for weekly synth (used for my sprint retros).
   - Commitment 3: Do two 60m focused deep work sessions (no Slack).

4) Measurement plan (quick, objective signals):
   - Primary signal: # of candidate prompts created (target >=6).
   - Secondary: # of focused slots completed (target 2).
   - Tertiary: Time saved next week from template reuse (qualitative note).

5) Quick experiments to run if time:
   - Try doing a morning 20-min write to capture raw thoughts vs evening tidy — record quality difference (3-point scale: noisy/useful/ready).
   - Pre-commit a 15-min review slot after every meeting to extract 1 action or insight.

6) Risks / blockers to watch:
   - Meeting creep. If >6 in a day, shut a non-essential calendar block.
   - Perfection trap — template must be "good enough" not perfect.

Notes to self (ragged):
- Use the "sprint template" in CONFLUENCE-ops/weekly-templates as seed; drop anything that feels heavy.
- If I don't hit primary signal by Thursday, escalate: cut one commitment and move to next week.
- This doc is intentionally messy. Capture the small wins and one clear lesson each Friday (two lines).

Friday retro prompt (3 min):
- 1 line: what actually moved the needle this week?
- 1 line: what wasted the most time?
- 1 line: next week's single sentence northline.

Unresolved questions (for follow-up):
- Should I track deep work completion in Notion or a simple checklist here? Leaning to keep it local in this file for velocity.
- Can I automate the candidate-prompt extraction with a small script (see JIRA-GOAL-221)? Add as backlog item if I hit 3 straight weeks of manual signal.

Action items (today):
- [ ] Drop calendar guard for two 60m slots (Mon/Wed).
- [ ] Run micro-audit on last 4 weeks of notes and tag candidates.
- [ ] Draft simple one-pager weekly-synth template and share with Jonah for quick feedback.

Log (live updates):
- 2025-01-09: Created skeleton. Hooked template to CONFLUENCE-ops.
- 2025-01-10: Did 1 deep slot (60m). Found 2 candidate prompts.
- 2025-01-13: Template drafted, sent to Jonah.
- 2025-01-15: Attempted morning write 3 days, quality noted as: noisy, useful, useful.

Micro-retrospective (end of week snapshot):
- Win: Shipping a tiny template removed the friction of weekly synth — saved ~20m on Friday.
- Learn: Morning write needs a tighter prompt to be consistently useful.

If this still exists in three weeks: assess automation idea and move repeated commitments into a recurring calendar habit.

References (quick links):
- CONFLUENCE-ops/weekly-templates (seed templates)
- JIRA-GOAL-221 (automation backlog)
- Slack: thread "weekly-synth" for feedback notes

End of page — keep this lean.
